question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

Nylon was among the first synthitic fibre made by man and is known for its toughness, strength and resistance to oil and grease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. synthitic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Synthitic" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "synthetic", meaning made by chemical synthesis; artificial, not natural. (कृत्रिम)

◦ Correct: Nylon was among the first synthetic fibres made by man ...

• Spelling key: SYN + THE + TIC (from "synthesis").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "toughness" (the quality of being strong and durable), "strength" (the state of being strong) and "resistance" (the ability to withstand something) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: synthesis (noun), synthesise (verb), synthetic (adjective). Synthetic fibres: nylon, polyester, acrylic, rayon (semi-synthetic); nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre (1935).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

The name, Khajuraho, has probably been derived from the word ‘Khajoor’, meaning date palm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Has been derived from" is the correct present perfect passive structure (has/have + been + V3), and the verb "derive" correctly takes the preposition "from" (derived from a source).

◦ Correct: The name, Khajuraho, has probably been derived from the word 'Khajoor' ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "be derived into" and Option 3 "derives into" use the wrong preposition — "derive" pairs with "from", never "into".

• Option 2 "derive at" is unidiomatic; we "arrive at" a conclusion but "derive from" a source.

NOTE

• Passive voice of the present perfect: has/have + been + past participle (has been derived, has been built). Fixed preposition pairs: derive from, originate from, arrive at, result in.

question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The robbers stabbed him by a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with a sharp knife.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The instrument used to do something takes the preposition "with", not "by". "By" is used for the doer (agent) of the action; "with" is used for the tool/instrument.

◦ Correct: The robbers stabbed him with a sharp knife and he started bleeding profusely on the spot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly changes the pronoun "him" to "her".

• Option 2 wrongly replaces "and" with "but" — there is no contrast between the two clauses.

• Option 3 "from the spot" is wrong; "on the spot" (immediately/at that very place) is the correct idiom.

NOTE

• Rule: Passive/instrumental use — "He was killed by the robber (agent) with a knife (instrument)." Remember: by + doer, with + instrument.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Tom will _________ the document to the office tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mail" (verb) means to send something by post or electronically. Sending a document to the office requires the verb "mail". (डाक से भेजना)

◦ Correct: Tom will mail the document to the office tomorrow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mall" (a large shopping centre), Option 2 "meal" (food eaten at one time) and Option 4 "male" (of the masculine sex) are homophone-like words that make no sense in the sentence.

NOTE

• Confusing homophones: mail (post) / male (masculine); meet / meat; week / weak. SSC often tests such similar-sounding words in fill-in-the-blank questions.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

You have spoilt / the little chance you / had at succeeding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands: "You have spoilt the little chance you had at succeeding."

◦ "You have spoilt" — correct present perfect (have + V3; "spoilt" is a valid British past participle of "spoil").

◦ "the little chance you" — "little" correctly modifies the uncountable-like sense of "chance", and "you had" is a proper contact (relative) clause with "that/which" understood.

◦ "had at succeeding" — "a chance at + gerund (succeeding)" is an accepted construction, e.g., "a chance at winning".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Spoil" has two correct past forms: spoilt (British) and spoiled (American).

• "Chance" can take "of + gerund", "at + gerund" or "to + infinitive": a chance of succeeding / a chance at succeeding / a chance to succeed.

NOTE

• In "error spotting" questions, do not force an error — if every part follows grammar rules, confidently mark "No error".

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The vital role played by women at home and in the struggle for freedom, advanced the case for female emancipation soon after the war was over.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Emancipation" means the act of setting free from legal, social or political restrictions; liberation. Its closest synonym is "freedom". (मुक्ति / स्वतंत्रता)

◦ Example: The emancipation/freedom of women gave them equal rights in society.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bondage" (slavery/captivity) is the antonym of emancipation.

• Option 3 "utility" (usefulness) and Option 4 "objectivity" (impartiality) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of emancipation: freedom, liberation, release, deliverance. Antonyms: bondage, slavery, servitude, subjugation. Related history fact: Abraham Lincoln's "Emancipation Proclamation" (1863) freed slaves in the USA.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

That question is / much difficult / but this one is / very easy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. much difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Much" cannot modify a positive-degree adjective like "difficult". The correct intensifier before a positive adjective is "very" — so it should be "very difficult".

◦ Correct: That question is very difficult but this one is very easy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "That question is", "but this one is" and "very easy" are all correct.

• "Much" is used before a comparative degree: "much more difficult", "much better", "much easier".

NOTE

• Intensifier rule: very + positive degree (very difficult), much + comparative degree (much more difficult). Also: "very" with present participles (very interesting), "much" with past participles (much admired).

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets.

The magician's performance was (captivating) and held the audience spellbound.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Boring.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Captivating" means holding one's attention completely; charming and fascinating. Its antonym is "boring", meaning dull and uninteresting. (मनमोहक का विलोम — उबाऊ/नीरस)

◦ Example: The captivating show became boring in its second half.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Fascinating", 3 "Enchanting" and 4 "Gripping" are all synonyms of captivating — a common SSC trap where three options are synonyms and only one is the true antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of captivating: fascinating, enchanting, gripping, mesmerising, spellbinding. Antonyms: boring, dull, tedious, monotonous, unattractive.

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: I went to watch a play with one of my friends.
option_2: A famous poet wrote that poem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He resides near an university.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "an" is used before a vowel sound, not merely a vowel letter. "University" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yoo"), so it takes "a" — "a university".

◦ Correct: He resides near a university.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 correctly uses "one of my friends" (one of + plural noun).

• Options 2 and 3 correctly use the articles "A famous poet" and "A dog".

NOTE

• Article choice depends on sound, not spelling: "a university, a European, a one-rupee note, a useful book" (consonant sounds) but "an hour, an honest man, an MLA, an umbrella" (vowel sounds).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Recieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Recieve" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "receive", meaning to get or be given something. (प्राप्त करना)

◦ Correct: I receive many letters every week.

• Spelling rule: "i before e, except after c" — after the letter "c", write "ei": re + cei + ve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Thief", "Believe" and "Relief" are all correctly spelt — in each, "ie" follows a letter other than "c", so "i before e" applies.

NOTE

• Words with "ei" after c: receive, deceive, conceive, perceive, ceiling. Words with "ie": believe, thief, relief, achieve, field. Exceptions to memorise: seize, weird, foreign, height.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I will not be able to ___________ my assignment in time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. complete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "to" (the infinitive marker), the base form (V1) of the verb is used — "to complete". The structure is "be able to + V1".

◦ Correct: I will not be able to complete my assignment in time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "completes" (third-person singular), Option 3 "completed" (past form/V2) and Option 4 "completing" (present participle) cannot follow the infinitive "to".

NOTE

• "Be able to + V1" expresses ability (like "can"): "will be able to complete", "was able to finish". Never use V2/V3/V-ing after the infinitive "to" in such structures.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the highlighted word.

His eloquent speech moved the audience to tears.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Expressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eloquent" means fluent, forceful and persuasive in speech or writing; effectively expressive. Its closest synonym is "expressive". (वाक्पटु / प्रभावशाली वक्ता)

◦ Example: The leader's eloquent/expressive speech inspired the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vernacular" (the local language of a region) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "Inarticulate" (unable to express oneself clearly) is the antonym of eloquent.

• Option 3 "Angry" is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of eloquent: expressive, articulate, fluent, persuasive, silver-tongued. Antonyms: inarticulate, tongue-tied, halting.

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

The grapes taste sweetest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sweet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Taste" is a linking verb (verb of sensation) and is followed by an adjective in the positive degree when no comparison is made. Since the sentence compares the grapes with nothing, the superlative "sweetest" is wrong — it should simply be "sweet".

◦ Correct: The grapes taste sweet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more sweeter" and Option 4 "most sweeter" are double comparatives/superlatives — always incorrect.

• Option 2 "sweeter" (comparative) needs "than" and a second item of comparison, which is absent.

NOTE

• Linking verbs of sensation — taste, smell, look, feel, sound — take an adjective, not an adverb: "The soup tastes good (not well)", "She looks beautiful", "The flowers smell sweet".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The intersection of nature conservation and social justice is evident in efforts to ensure that marginalised communities and other backward classes should have equal access to natural reserves.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. apparent in endeavours to guarantee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The substitute must keep the same meaning as "evident in efforts to ensure":

◦ "evident" = "apparent" (clearly seen or understood),

◦ "efforts" = "endeavours" (attempts/exertions),

◦ "ensure" = "guarantee" (to make certain).

◦ Correct: ... is apparent in endeavours to guarantee that marginalised communities ... have equal access ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 changes "ensure" to "redesign" (to plan again) — meaning altered.

• Option 2 "Unclear" is the opposite of "evident".

• Option 4 changes "ensure" to "recollect" (to remember) — meaning altered.

NOTE

• Synonym chains useful for SSC: evident–apparent–obvious–manifest; effort–endeavour–attempt–exertion; ensure–guarantee–secure–make certain.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Her amicable nature made it easy for her to forge positive relationships.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Friendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amicable" means having a friendly and pleasant manner; characterised by goodwill. Its closest synonym is "friendly". (मैत्रीपूर्ण / मिलनसार)

◦ Example: Her amicable/friendly nature helped her build positive relationships.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sad" (unhappy) and Option 4 "Attentive" (paying attention) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "Aggressive" (hostile/forceful) is close to an antonym of amicable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amicable: friendly, cordial, genial, affable, amiable. Antonyms: hostile, unfriendly, aggressive. Distinguish: amicable (of relations/settlements — an amicable divorce) vs amiable (of a person's nature).

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

The play was shortened by the ___________ of two scenes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. omission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Omission" means the act of leaving out or excluding something. The play could be shortened only by leaving out (omitting) two scenes. (छोड़ देना / लोप)

◦ Correct: The play was shortened by the omission of two scenes.

• Spelling key: O + MIS + SION (one "m", double "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "addition" is correctly spelt but reverses the meaning — adding scenes would lengthen, not shorten, the play.

• Option 3 "ommision" (correct: omission) and Option 4 "insirtion" (correct: insertion) are misspelt.

NOTE

• Word family: omit (verb) – omission (noun) – omitted/omitting (double "t" in inflected forms). Antonyms of omission: addition, inclusion, insertion.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As 'brutal' is synonymous to 'harsh'

, 'naive' is synonymous to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. simple.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Naive" means innocent, unsophisticated and lacking worldly experience or judgement. Its closest synonym is "simple". (भोला-भाला / सरल)

◦ Just as brutal = harsh, so naive = simple.

◦ Example: The naive/simple villager believed every word of the trickster.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "wise" (having good judgement) and Option 4 "worldly" (experienced in the ways of the world) are antonyms of naive.

• Option 2 "hospitable" (welcoming to guests) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of naive: simple, innocent, artless, ingenuous, credulous, gullible. Antonyms: worldly, shrewd, sophisticated, experienced.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hornet's nest
option_4: A house built with great difficulty
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A troublesome or hazardous situation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hornet's nest" means a very troublesome, dangerous or hazardous situation, especially one that provokes strong angry reactions. To "stir up a hornet's nest" is to create a lot of trouble. (मुसीबत/झंझट भरी स्थिति)

◦ Example: His controversial remark stirred up a hornet's nest in the office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "A bee's nest" takes the idiom literally — idioms must never be interpreted literally.

• Options 1 and 4 do not convey the sense of provoked trouble.

NOTE

• Related idioms of trouble: "open a can of worms" (create a complicated problem), "in hot water" (in trouble), "add fuel to the fire" (worsen a situation).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the standard for the company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. up to the mark.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "up to the mark" means meeting the required or expected standard. It exactly substitutes "up to the standard". (अपेक्षित स्तर के अनुरूप)

◦ Correct: The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the mark for the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "an uphill task" (a very difficult job), Option 3 "up and doing" (busy and active) and Option 4 "under the nose" (right in front of someone) do not fit the sense of "meeting a standard".

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "up to scratch", "up to par", "measure up" — all mean reaching the required standard; "not up to the mark" = below the expected standard.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.

Mukta requested Nikita to share the picture taken during the wedding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is already correct: "requested + object + to + V1" is the standard pattern — "Mukta requested Nikita to share the picture ...".

◦ The simple past "requested" suits the completed action, and the participle phrase "taken during the wedding" correctly modifies "the picture".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will requests" wrongly adds "-s" to the base verb after "will".

• Option 2 "requesting" leaves the sentence without a finite main verb.

• Option 3 "requested Nikita for share" is unidiomatic — "request someone to do something" or "request for something (noun)", never "for share".

NOTE

• Pattern verbs like request/ask/advise/order take: verb + object + to-infinitive — "She asked him to leave", "He advised me to wait".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prefer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prefer" means to like one thing/place more than another; to choose by liking. Saltwater crocodiles are called estuarine crocodiles because they prefer (like/choose) to live in mangrove-lined rivers. (पसंद करना)

◦ Correct: ... as they prefer to live in mangrove-lined rivers.

• "Prefer + to-infinitive" (prefer to live) is the correct structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "defer" (to postpone; to yield), Option 2 "refer" (to mention/consult) and Option 3 "differ" (to be unlike) do not fit the sense of habitat choice.

NOTE

• Watch these look-alike verbs: prefer (like better), defer (postpone), refer (mention), differ (disagree/be different), infer (conclude), confer (discuss/bestow).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. largest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clue "reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than ... Komodo dragon" shows that the passage is talking about size. Hence "the largest living reptile" is correct. (सबसे बड़ा)

◦ Correct: They're the largest living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fattest" (having most fat), Option 3 "broadest" (widest) and Option 4 "poorest" do not match the comparison of overall size/length.

• The superlative "largest" with "the" is used because the crocodile is compared with all living reptiles.

NOTE

• GK link: the saltwater (estuarine) crocodile is indeed the largest living reptile; the Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard (found in Indonesia).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Historically.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Historically" means in the past; throughout history. The sentence uses the past tense ("crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago") and the following lines cite the early 20th century and the 1950s — clearly a historical account. (ऐतिहासिक रूप से)

◦ Correct: Historically, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Abysmally" (extremely badly), Option 3 "Fanatically" (with extreme enthusiasm) and Option 4 "acrobatically" (with gymnastic agility) make no sense as sentence openers here.

NOTE

• Sentence adverbs like Historically, Traditionally, Generally, Interestingly are set off by a comma and comment on the whole sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. records.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Records" means written or documented accounts of past events. We have "records of attacks on humans" — i.e., documented evidence of such attacks from the early 20th century. (अभिलेख / दस्तावेज़)

◦ Correct: We have records of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "recipes" (cooking instructions), Option 3 "regiments" (army units) and Option 4 "residues" (remainders left behind) do not fit documented history.

• "Records of something" is the correct collocation.

NOTE

• "Record" collocations: keep a record, on record, records of attacks/events, record-keeping. Compare: record (noun — document), record (verb — to register).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Saltwater crocodiles are also known as estuarine crocodiles, as they (1)_____________ to live in mangrove-lined rivers. They’re the (2)_________________ living reptile, reaching up to seven metres in length: far larger than Indonesia’s famous Komodo dragon, which tops out at three metres. (3)______________________, crocodiles lived throughout the Indonesian archipelago. We have (4)_________________ of attacks on humans in Bali from the early 20th century and across much of Java until the 1950s. Even Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, had crocodile’s (5)____________________ in many rivers running through the city.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. residence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Residence" means the place where someone/something lives; dwelling. Jakarta's rivers were places where crocodiles lived — their "residence". (निवास)

◦ Correct: Even Indonesia's capital, Jakarta, had crocodile's residence in many rivers running through the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "relevance" (connection with the matter), Option 2 "resistance" (opposition) and Option 4 "remembrance" (memory) do not convey "living/dwelling in the rivers".

NOTE

• Word family: reside (verb — to live), residence (noun — dwelling), resident (noun/adjective — one who lives in a place), residential (adjective — of housing).

question: Which Article states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to abide by the constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51A (a).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(a) of the Constitution lays down the first Fundamental Duty: every citizen of India shall abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem. (अनुच्छेद 51A(a) — पहला मौलिक कर्तव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, in Part IV-A (Article 51A).

• Originally 10 duties; the 11th duty (education for children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

• Article 52 — there shall be a President of India; Article 14 — equality before law; Article 54 — election of the President.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) and were borrowed from the Constitution of the USSR (Russia).

question:
Which of the following statements about phylum Arthropoda are correct?

A. Animals of Arthropoda have joint appendages.

B. They have compounds eyes.

C. These make up the majority of all animals on earth.

D. The mode of reproduction in all Arthropods is vegetative.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A, B and C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement A — Correct: the very name Arthropoda means "jointed legs/appendages" (Greek: arthron = joint, podos = foot).

• Statement B — Correct: arthropods (e.g., insects like the housefly and prawn) have compound eyes made of many small visual units (ommatidia).

• Statement C — Correct: Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom — over two-thirds of all known animal species are arthropods.

• Statement D — Incorrect: arthropods reproduce sexually (males and females are usually separate); reproduction is not vegetative. Vegetative reproduction is a mode of asexual reproduction in plants.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Features of Arthropoda: chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body (head, thorax, abdomen), open circulatory system (haemocoel), jointed appendages.

• Examples: cockroach, prawn, crab, spider, scorpion, butterfly, Apis (honey bee).

NOTE

• Largest phylum — Arthropoda; largest class within it — Insecta. (संधिपाद — सबसे बड़ा संघ)

question: Which of the following is the principal strategy adopted by National Literacy Mission for the eradication of illiteracy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Total Literacy Campaign.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Total Literacy Campaign (TLC)" was the principal strategy of the National Literacy Mission (NLM) for eradicating adult illiteracy. It was an area-specific, time-bound, volunteer-based campaign to impart functional literacy. (सम्पूर्ण साक्षरता अभियान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National Literacy Mission was launched in 1988 to impart functional literacy to non-literates in the 15–35 age group.

• The Ernakulam district of Kerala (1990) was the first district in India declared fully literate through the TLC; Kerala became the first fully literate state (1991).

• Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001) deals with universal elementary education for children (6–14 years), not adult literacy.

NOTE

• The NLM was later recast as Saakshar Bharat (2009); the current adult-literacy programme is the New India Literacy Programme (ULLAS, 2022), aligned with NEP 2020.

question: The construction of Humayun's tomb was completed by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Biga Begum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Humayun's Tomb (Delhi) was commissioned and its construction completed by Biga Begum (Bega Begum, also known as Haji Begum), the senior widow of Emperor Humayun. It was completed around 1571–72. (बेगा बेगम / हाजी बेगम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The tomb was designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas (and his son Sayyid Muhammad).

• It is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, built in the Charbagh (four-quartered garden) style, and served as a precursor/model for the Taj Mahal.

• It is built of red sandstone with white marble and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

NOTE

• Humayun (r. 1530–40 and 1555–56) died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library Sher Mandal in Purana Qila, Delhi.

question: The Patli Dun is associated with which physiographic division of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Himalayan Mountains.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Patli Dun" is a dun (longitudinal valley) lying between the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and the Shiwalik ranges — hence it belongs to the Himalayan Mountains physiographic division. (पाटली दून — हिमालय पर्वत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Duns are flat-floored structural valleys between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalaya. Famous duns: Dehra Dun (the largest), Kotli Dun, Patli Dun and Kothri Dun.

• Patli Dun lies in Uttarakhand, drained by the Ramganga river, and houses the Corbett National Park area.

• India's physiographic divisions: the Himalayan Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.

NOTE

• Himalayan ranges from north to south: Greater Himalaya (Himadri) → Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) → Shiwaliks (Outer Himalaya) — duns lie between the last two.

question:
Consider the following statements in the context of the Mughal Rule.

1. The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571.

2. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556.

3. Maharana Pratap Singh of Mewar was a contemporary of Babur.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 — Correct: the Mansabdari system — a grading system that fixed the rank (mansab), salary and military obligations of officers — was introduced by Akbar (1571). Ranks were expressed as zat (personal status) and sawar (cavalry to be maintained).

• Statement 2 — Correct: the Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556) was fought between Akbar (under Bairam Khan) and Hemu (Hem Chandra Vikramaditya); Hemu was defeated.

• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Maharana Pratap of Mewar was a contemporary of Akbar, not Babur — he fought Akbar's forces at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Man Singh and Asaf Khan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur (r. 1526–1530) fought the First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi and the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga (Maharana Pratap's grandfather-generation ruler of Mewar).

• The word "mansab" means rank/position; mansabdars were paid either in cash (naqdi) or through jagirs.

NOTE

• Battles of Panipat: 1526 (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi), 1556 (Akbar vs Hemu), 1761 (Marathas vs Ahmad Shah Abdali).

question: Who built Sudarshan lake in Junagarh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pushyagupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sudarshan lake (Sudarshana reservoir) at Girnar hills, Junagarh (Gujarat) was built by Pushyagupta, the provincial governor of Chandragupta Maurya in Saurashtra. (सुदर्शन झील — पुष्यगुप्त)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• This information comes from the Junagarh (Girnar) rock inscription of Rudradaman I (c. 150 CE) — the earliest long inscription in chaste Sanskrit.

• The lake was later provided with conduits under Ashoka (by Tushaspha, his Yavana governor), repaired by the Shaka ruler Rudradaman I after storm damage, and repaired again under Skandagupta (by his governor Parnadatta/Chakrapalita).

NOTE

• The Sudarshan lake is a classic SSC theme: built — Pushyagupta (Mauryan); repaired — Rudradaman I (Shaka); repaired again — Skandagupta (Gupta).

question: Which of the following dance categories is NOT considered for an award of the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vilasini Natyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vilasini Natyam (a temple-dance tradition of Andhra Pradesh revived by Swapnasundari) is NOT among the classical dance categories recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi for its awards. (विलासिनी नाट्यम — मान्यता प्राप्त शास्त्रीय नृत्य श्रेणी नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (established 1953, headquarters New Delhi) is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

• The Akademi confers classical status/awards on dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya (and also Chhau as a major tradition).

• Sattriya (Assam) was the latest addition to the classical list (recognised in 2000).

NOTE

• The Ministry of Culture recognises 8 classical dances; the Sangeet Natak Akademi's highest honour is the Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna).

question: Which of the following personalities had the key role in fighting against the British East India Company in the Battle of Porto Novo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hyder Ali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Porto Novo (1 July 1781), fought at Porto Novo (Parangipettai, Tamil Nadu) during the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–84), saw Hyder Ali of Mysore fighting against the British East India Company forces led by Sir Eyre Coote; Hyder Ali was defeated in this battle. (हैदर अली — पोर्टो नोवो का युद्ध)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Hyder Ali (father of Tipu Sultan) became the de facto ruler of Mysore in 1761; he died in 1782 during the war, after which Tipu Sultan continued the fight.

• The Second Anglo-Mysore War ended with the Treaty of Mangalore (1784), signed by Tipu Sultan — one of the few treaties where an Indian power dictated terms to the British.

• Maharaja Ranjit Singh was the Sikh ruler of Punjab; Alamgir II was a later Mughal emperor (1754–59).

NOTE

• Anglo-Mysore Wars: First (1767–69), Second (1780–84), Third (1790–92, Treaty of Seringapatam), Fourth (1799 — Tipu Sultan died defending Srirangapatna).

question: What is the primary function of the notochord in chordates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "notochord" is a flexible rod-like structure present on the dorsal side of chordates; its primary function is to provide skeletal support to the body and a firm structure for muscle attachment. (पृष्ठरज्जु — सहारा/आधार प्रदान करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The notochord is formed from the mesoderm and lies between the nerve cord and the alimentary canal.

• In vertebrates, the notochord is replaced (partly or wholly) by the vertebral column (backbone) during development.

• Chordate characteristics: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits and post-anal tail.

NOTE

• All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates (e.g., Amphioxus/lancelet retains the notochord throughout life).

question: Manipuri Raas Leela, a renowned form of classical dance, was created by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharaja Bhagyachandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Manipuri Raas Leela, the celebrated classical dance of Manipur depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna, was created/introduced by Maharaja Bhagyachandra (Rajarshi Bhagyachandra) in the 18th century (c. 1779). (महाराजा भाग्यचंद्र — मणिपुरी रासलीला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Maharaja Bhagyachandra is also credited with designing the distinctive Kumil (barrel-shaped skirt) costume of Manipuri dance.

• Manipuri dance is deeply linked with Vaishnavism; its tandava and lasya aspects appear in forms like Pung cholom (drum dance).

• Siddhendra Yogi is associated with Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh); Birju Maharaj was a legendary Kathak exponent; Sage Bharata wrote the Natya Shastra.

NOTE

• The Sankirtana of Manipur (ritual singing and drumming) is inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2013).

question: In February 2023, UNICEF India announced the appointment of which celebrated Bollywood star as a National Ambassador for Child Rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ayushmann Khurrana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2023, UNICEF India appointed the Bollywood actor Ayushmann Khurrana as its National Ambassador for Child Rights — to champion every child's right to protection, health and education. (आयुष्मान खुराना — यूनिसेफ राष्ट्रीय राजदूत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ayushmann Khurrana had earlier worked with UNICEF as a celebrity advocate for its "For Every Child" campaign against violence towards children.

• UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) — established 1946, headquarters New York; won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

• UNICEF works for children's health, nutrition, education, immunisation and protection worldwide.

NOTE

• Other noted UNICEF ambassadors from India have included Amitabh Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra and Sachin Tendulkar (in goodwill/advocacy roles).

question: Fuels that are derived from fossils are preserved only in which kind of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rocks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) and fossils in general are found/preserved only in "sedimentary rocks". These rocks form by the deposition and compaction of sediments in layers (strata), which trap and preserve the remains of dead plants and animals. (अवसादी चट्टानें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Coal formed from buried vegetation in swampy basins; petroleum and natural gas formed from marine organisms trapped between impermeable sedimentary layers.

• Examples of sedimentary rocks: sandstone, limestone, shale, conglomerate, coal.

• Igneous rocks (volcanic/plutonic) form from cooled magma — their heat destroys organic remains; metamorphic rocks form under heat and pressure, which also destroys fossils.

NOTE

• Rock types: Igneous (primary rocks — granite, basalt), Sedimentary (layered, fossil-bearing — limestone), Metamorphic (changed form — marble from limestone, slate from shale).

question: Select the imbalanced chemical equation from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 HClO4 + P4O10 → 4 H3PO4 + 6 Cl2O7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A balanced equation must have an equal number of atoms of every element on both sides (Law of Conservation of Mass).

• Check Option 2: 6 HClO4 + P4O10 → 4 H3PO4 + 6 Cl2O7

◦ H: left = 6, right = 4 × 3 = 12 — NOT equal.

◦ O: left = 24 + 10 = 34, right = 16 + 42 = 58 — NOT equal.

◦ Hence this equation is imbalanced. (The balanced form is 12 HClO4 + P4O10 → 4 H3PO4 + 6 Cl2O7.)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: K 10=10, Cl 10=10, O 30=30, P 12=12 — balanced.

• Option 3: Ca 3=3, Cl 6=6, Na 6=6, P 2=2, O 8=8 — balanced.

• Option 4: Hg 3=3, O 14=14, H 12=12, P 2=2 — balanced.

NOTE

• The Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier) states that matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction — this is why equations are balanced by adjusting coefficients, never by changing formulae.

question: Yashodhara Dalmia is the author of which famous book?
option_3: The Painted World of the Warlis
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Painted World of the Warlis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Painted World of the Warlis (1988)" was written by the noted art historian and curator Yashodhara Dalmia. The book documents the life and ritual Warli painting tradition of the Warli tribe. (यशोधरा डालमिया — वारली चित्रकला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Warli painting is a tribal art form of the Warli tribe of Maharashtra (Palghar/Thane region), using white pigment (rice paste) on mud walls with simple geometric shapes — circles, triangles and squares — depicting daily life, the Tarpa dance and marriage rituals (Chauk).

• Jivya Soma Mashe was the most celebrated Warli artist (Padma Shri, 2011).

• Yashodhara Dalmia has also written on modern Indian art, e.g., "Amrita Sher-Gil: A Life".

NOTE

• Famous folk/tribal art forms: Warli (Maharashtra), Madhubani (Bihar), Pattachitra (Odisha), Gond (Madhya Pradesh), Phad (Rajasthan), Kalamkari (Andhra Pradesh).

question: Who among the following was appointed as the director-general in the Directorate General of Civil Aviation in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Dev Dutt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2023, Vikram Dev Dutt (an AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, earlier CMD of Air India Asset Holdings) was appointed as the Director-General of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). (विक्रम देव दत्त — डीजीसीए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The DGCA is the regulatory body for civil aviation in India under the Ministry of Civil Aviation; it deals with safety, licensing of pilots, airworthiness and air-transport regulations. Headquarters: New Delhi.

• At that time, Ajay Kumar Bhalla was the Union Home Secretary, Rajiv Gauba the Cabinet Secretary and Dr. P. K. Mishra the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Related aviation bodies: AAI (Airports Authority of India — infrastructure), BCAS (Bureau of Civil Aviation Security — security), AERA (economic regulation of major airports), DGCA (safety regulation).

question: Which of the following does NOT figure among the themes of 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Health@75.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav" — the celebration of 75 years of India's independence — is built around five themes: Freedom Struggle, Ideas@75, Achievements@75, Actions@75 and Resolve@75. "Health@75" is NOT one of its themes. (आज़ादी का अमृत महोत्सव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Mahotsav was launched by the Prime Minister on 12 March 2021 with the flag-off of the Dandi March re-enactment from Sabarmati Ashram, 75 weeks before 15 August 2022.

• It concluded with "Meri Maati Mera Desh" campaign in 2023.

• Programmes like Har Ghar Tiranga (hoisting the national flag at every home) were part of the celebrations.

NOTE

• The five themes are officially described as the "Panch Pran" pillars of the celebration: Freedom Struggle, Ideas@75, Resolve@75, Actions@75 and Achievements@75 — remember there is no Health@75.

question: Which country hosted the Football World Cup, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qatar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The FIFA World Cup 2022 was hosted by "Qatar" (November–December 2022) — the first World Cup held in the Middle East/an Arab country and the first played in November–December instead of the usual June–July. (फीफा विश्व कप 2022 — कतर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Argentina won the title, defeating France on penalties (3-3, 4-2 on penalties) in the final at the Lusail Stadium — Argentina's third title.

• Lionel Messi won the Golden Ball; Kylian Mbappé (France) won the Golden Boot with 8 goals; the mascot was La'eeb.

• FIFA World Cup 2026 will be jointly hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico (48 teams).

NOTE

• FIFA — Fédération Internationale de Football Association; founded 1904, headquarters Zurich, Switzerland. Most World Cup titles: Brazil (5).

question: Who explained the system of classifying musical instruments into Tata, Sushira, Avanaddha and Ghana in his treatise 'Natya Shastra' in the early 2nd century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharata Muni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharata Muni, in his treatise "Natya Shastra", classified musical instruments into four categories: Tata (stringed), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (membrane/percussion) and Ghana (solid — cymbals, etc.). (भरत मुनि — नाट्यशास्त्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Natya Shastra is the foundational Sanskrit text on dance, drama and music (natya), and also expounds the theory of rasa (aesthetic sentiment).

• Examples of the four classes: Tata — sitar, veena, sarod; Sushira — flute, shehnai, nadaswaram; Avanaddha — tabla, mridangam, dholak; Ghana — manjira, jaltarang, ghatam.

• Sarngadeva wrote the "Sangita Ratnakara" (13th century), another key musical treatise; Swami Haridas was the guru of Tansen.

NOTE

• The Natya Shastra is often called the "fifth Veda (Natyaveda)"; classical dance forms trace their grammar (mudras, abhinaya) to it.

question: Which of the following statements is true about Micro Finance institutions?
option_1: Type of banking service provided to employed
option_2: Service provided to High income people only
option_3: Majority of microfinancing operations occur in developing countries
solution_text:
The correct answer is Majority of microfinancing operations occur in developing countries.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance is a banking/financial service that provides small loans (micro-credit) and other financial services to low-income groups, the unemployed and small entrepreneurs who lack access to formal banking. The majority of microfinancing operations occur in developing countries such as India, Bangladesh, Uganda and Indonesia. (सूक्ष्म वित्त — विकासशील देशों में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 2 are wrong — microfinance targets the poor/low-income and unemployed, not only the employed or high-income people; Option 4 is wrong — it provides micro (small) loans, not jumbo loans.

• Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh pioneered modern microfinance through the Grameen Bank (1983) and won the Nobel Peace Prize 2006.

• In India, microfinance works through Self-Help Groups (SHG)-Bank linkage (NABARD, 1992) and Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs); MUDRA (2015) refinances micro-enterprise loans up to Rs. 10 lakh.

NOTE

• The RBI regulates NBFC-MFIs; microfinance loans are typically collateral-free small loans aimed at financial inclusion and women's empowerment.

question: What is the rank of India in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 111.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the "Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023", India ranked 111th out of 125 countries, with a score of 28.7, placing it in the "serious" hunger category. (वैश्विक भुखमरी सूचकांक 2023 — भारत 111वें स्थान पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The GHI is published jointly by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany).

• It is based on four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality (children under five).

• In GHI 2023, India's neighbours ranked better: Pakistan (102), Bangladesh (81), Nepal (69), Sri Lanka (60). The Government of India disputed the index's methodology.

NOTE

• GHI severity scale: low (below 9.9), moderate (10–19.9), serious (20–34.9), alarming (35–49.9), extremely alarming (50+).

question: In which year did India first participate in the Paralympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1968.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India made its first appearance at the Paralympic Games in 1968, at the Tel Aviv (Israel) Summer Paralympics. (भारत की पहली पैरालंपिक भागीदारी — 1968)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's first Paralympic medal came in 1972 (Heidelberg), when swimmer Murlikant Petkar won gold in the 50 m freestyle (with a world record).

• Deepa Malik became the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic medal (silver, shot put, Rio 2016).

• At the Paris 2024 Paralympics, India won a record 29 medals (7 gold); at Tokyo 2020, 19 medals (5 gold, including Avani Lekhara's shooting gold).

NOTE

• The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960; the movement grew out of the Stoke Mandeville Games started by Sir Ludwig Guttmann (1948). The Paralympic motto is "Spirit in Motion".

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment and duties of the Attorney-General of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 76.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 76 of the Constitution deals with the Attorney-General of India (AGI) — the highest law officer of the country. He is appointed by the President and must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court. (अनुच्छेद 76 — भारत का महान्यायवादी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The AGI gives legal advice to the Government of India, holds office during the pleasure of the President, and has the right of audience in all courts of India (Article 76) and the right to speak in either House of Parliament (Article 88), though he cannot vote.

• The first Attorney-General was M. C. Setalvad; the current AGI (since October 2022) is R. Venkataramani.

• Article 74 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President; Article 80 — composition of the Rajya Sabha; Article 81 — composition of the Lok Sabha; Article 165 — Advocate-General of a State.

NOTE

• The Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) is under Article 148; do not confuse the Attorney-General (Article 76) with the Advocate-General (Article 165) or the Solicitor-General (a non-constitutional post).

question: Which of following organisations sought to revive Vedic learning and combine it with modern education in the sciences?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Arya Samaj", founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, sought to revive Vedic learning — with the slogan "Go back to the Vedas" — and to combine it with modern education in the sciences, notably through the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) institutions. (आर्य समाज — वेदों की ओर लौटो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Swami Dayanand's book "Satyarth Prakash" contains his teachings; he condemned idol worship, caste rigidity, child marriage and untouchability, and promoted shuddhi (reconversion) and women's education.

• The first DAV College was established at Lahore in 1886 (Lala Hansraj); the Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar (1902) stream emphasised traditional Vedic education.

• Brahmo Samaj — Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1828); Prarthana Samaj — Atmaram Pandurang (1867, Bombay); Satyashodhak Samaj — Jyotiba Phule (1873, Pune).

NOTE

• Arya Samaj's ten principles centre on the Vedas as the scripture of true knowledge; it played a major role in social reform and the freedom-era awakening in Punjab and north India.

question: In which state is the ‘slash and burn’ agriculture known as ‘Dahiya’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Slash and burn (shifting) agriculture" is known as "Dahiya" in Madhya Pradesh (also called Bewar there). In this primitive subsistence farming, a forest patch is cleared and burnt, crops are grown, and the plot is abandoned once fertility declines. (दहिया — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Local names of shifting cultivation in India: Jhum (Assam/North-East), Podu/Penda (Andhra Pradesh/Odisha), Bewar/Dahiya (Madhya Pradesh), Kumari (Western Ghats/Kerala), Valre/Waltre (Rajasthan), Khil (Himalayan belt), Kuruwa (Jharkhand).

• World names: Milpa (Mexico), Roca (Brazil), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Masole (Congo/Central Africa).

• It is also called "slash and burn" because vegetation is cut (slashed) and burnt to add ash to the soil.

NOTE

• Shifting cultivation causes deforestation and soil erosion; governments promote settled (terrace) farming as an alternative. Jhum cycle shortening has worsened land degradation in the North-East.
